text:
alex: kicking off interleaved runs — synthetic traffic vs replay harness across us-west/us-east. KV cache warm and cold, kernel v2 vs v3, batching heuristics toggled. looking for apples-to-apples numbers. anyone object?
mira: +1. can you confirm replay seed and request-time distributions match the synthetic profile? last time they drifted and it skewed p95.
alex: good call. i'll pin the replay seed and also use the sampled sequence-length histogram from prod to drive synthetic.
jonathan: remember to snapshot KV cache state for warm runs. the replay harness can restore prefixes but our synthetic driver was just hitting empty caches before — huge difference.
sam: logging a small checklist: 1) same model weights & quantization (v1.4-q4) 2) same kernel build (gcc/clang flags) 3) identical batch-window logic 4) same routing policy + region weights.
leo: question: when we do multi-region, should we run cross-region RTT emulation or real infra? last round used netem which slightly under-penalized tail latency.
mira: prefer real infra if possible. netem for quick experiments but final apples-to-apples should be between identical instance types in different regions with real routing.
replay-harness-bot: started replay run 1769507777-1: us-west primary, us-east fallback, 10k reqs/s, seed=42, kv_state=warm
alex: posting initial profiler snippet — main hotspots around matmul kernel selection fallback on seq_len>2048. p50 diff small, p95 +18ms on v3.
jonathan: can you paste the flamegraph? might be kernel selection loop thrashing when batch sizes vary.
alex: here's a small excerpt:
```
hotspot: select_kernel_for_op()
  - check fast_path (matched 64x64)
  - fallback to generic matmul_kernel_fp16
  - compile_cache_miss -> compile_kernels()
```
mira: compile_cache_miss is bad. did the new kernel cache key include batch-dim + seq-dim? that would explode variants.
sam: it did, and that was intentional to avoid wrong kernels. but we can normalize keys (cap seq to nearest power-of-two bucket) to reduce churn.
leo: batching heuristic note: current window is 5ms; under synthetic burst patterns we see suboptimal micro-batches (many tiny batches) — increase to 10ms for high-throughput paths?
nina: be careful — increasing window helps throughput but spikes p99 when KV misses are frequent.
alex: observed behaviour: during region-drain (us-west node cordon), routing moved ~12% traffic to us-east and we saw p95 increase ~40ms for affected requests. fallback model (smaller fp16 quant) was used for ~7% of requests — latency higher but error rate lower.
jonathan: that suggests routing cutoff and fallback policy timing are too aggressive. prefer progressive spillover with warm-start of KV caches in target region.
mira: agree. suggested change: when draining, pre-warm 10% of traffic to target with cached prefixes replayed before shifting live traffic.
sam: action items: alex runs interleaved 3x (seed=42, 7am window), mira updates kernel-key normalization branch, jonathan prepares KV snapshot/restore hook, leo runs 6hr soak across both regions with real traffic replay.
alex: starting run #2: synthetic driver mirrored seq_hist and prefix distribution, same kernel binary, batching_window=10ms. launching now.
ops-bot: deploy notice: kernel-key-normalize branch deployed to staging at 1769508000
mira: after kernel-key-normalize on staging, compile_cache_miss rate dropped 87%. p95 decreased ~12ms on the same workload.
leo: one more test suggestion: run with disabled fallback (force same model) to measure pure routing latency vs model-change cost.
sam: good idea. that'll give us delta_model_latency = p95_with_fallback - p95_no_fallback.
alex: summary so far: 1) kernel-key explosion caused compile churn and tail latency 2) batching window tuning trades off throughput vs KV-miss tails 3) region-drain without pre-warm causes large p95 spike 4) fallback model reduces errors but adds latency; need smarter progressive fallback.
nina: +1 on progressive fallback. also add telemetry: tag requests with cache_hotness bucket so we can split p95 by cache state.
jonathan: assigning: i'll own KV snapshot/restore PR and test harness hook. ETA EOD tomorrow.
alex: i'll run the apples-to-apples matrix and upload consolidated CSV to /runbook/perf/1769507777-results.csv when done. aim for reproducible commands in README.
mira: linking the small config snippet to standardize runs:
```
{ "seed": 42,
  "batching_window_ms": 10,
  "kernel_binary": "prod/v3.2",
  "quant": "v1.4-q4",
  "kv_warm": true,
  "region_weights": {"us-west":0.88, "us-east":0.12}
}
```
alex: cool. plan: one final long run with kernel-key-normalize + batching 10ms + pre-warm on drain simulation. then propose config changes for staging traffic policy.
sam: thanks all. please call out any perf regressions in the CSV with the exact git sha so we can roll back quickly. :thumbsup:
alex: noted. will include git_shas per run. closing thread for now, will post results link when full run completes.
